_instructions: Rate each team's offensive coordinator/play-caller on a 1-5 scale. Use team abbreviations as keys. Tier 5 = elite scheme and player utilization, Tier 1 = poor. Missing teams default to tier 3 (neutral). Update as coaching staffs change.

_tiers.1: Poor — rigid scheme, misuses personnel, reactive rather than creative
_tiers.2: Below average — inconsistent utilization, limited creativity
_tiers.3: Average — competent but no clear edge in player deployment
_tiers.4: Above average — creative, adapts to personnel strengths, creates advantages
_tiers.5: Elite — maximizes each player's strengths, unpredictable, scheme-driven production

SF.notes: Gold standard for WR/RB utilization, motion-heavy, creates separation by design

MIA.notes: Shanahan disciple, elite at using speed and mismatch concepts

TEN.notes: Strong track record developing skill players in Cincinnati

HOU.notes: Shanahan tree, creative usage, Stroud-Diggs connection a key test

PHI.notes: Pass-heavy, creative route combinations, good TE usage

LAR.notes: HC/de facto OC, motion-heavy west coast, strong TE and RB usage

KC.notes: Mahomes elevates scheme above its design ceiling

DAL.notes: Conservative, run-first, limits ceiling of pass catchers

NYJ.notes: Historically poor utilization of skill talent
